1.text:
For twenty-five days, the Pasakoni boat goes on a steady way to its home port of Palakesi...
'A thousand greetings, Lon Wupu, I am Mawu...'
His warning is cut short by the blade of Mawu's small knife...

choices.choice_1_fight: Get on your feet and fight against these very great numbers
choices.choice_1_surrender: Give yourself up to Mawu and his men of war

6.text: The oil is made from the fruit of the Lanuma tree. It makes the skin quiet and free from pain when rubbed in.

choices.choice_6_rub: Rub the Lanuma oil into your skin
choices.choice_6_skip: Make a decision not to use the oil

8.text: You put all your Kai power into finding the number that will open the door... Take 2 ENDURANCE points from your full number.

14.text: You step into a clear half-ball room... You have found your taken things.

choices.choice_14_search: Look through the room for good things

16.text: You run into the room under the house and lock the door with the iron bar...

choices.choice_16_grille: Go away from the room under the house by the iron frame
choices.choice_16_fight: Keep in the room under the house and get ready for fight

17.text: It takes a long time for the fear and bad feeling in the stomach to go away...

choices.choice_17_west: Go on along the west deep water way
choices.choice_17_north: Turn north into the new deep hole
choices.choice_17_south: Go south along the new deep hole

19.text: You put up the head cover of your Kai coat to keep your face in the dark as you go near the guards...

choices.choice_19_bribe: Give the guards two Bag Things
choices.choice_19_leave: Go away from the door in the wall and look for another way in

26.text: Looking through the key hole, you can see that the lock is strange...

choices.choice_26_break: Make an attempt to break down the door
choices.choice_26_leave: Go away from the door and go to the steps

30.text: You go past many high arched doors looking out over the east town wall...

choices.choice_30_ledge: Keep out of sight outside on the narrow shelf
choices.choice_30_attack: Make an attack on the guards as they walk past

33.text: You cut into the dirt-covered floor and uncover a large metal ring...

choices.choice_33_fight: Get on your feet and fight the Sanasim

34.text: No matter how hard you try to get a picture of the machine... Take 1 ENDURANCE point away.

choices.choice_34_break: Make an attempt to break down the door
choices.choice_34_leave: Go away from the door and go to the steps

39.text: The man is saying things that are not true. He has knowledge that other guards are certain to come...

choices.choice_39_question: Go on put questions to him
choices.choice_39_kill: Make a decision to put him to death

41.text: You make your mouth full of oil but cannot make yourself send it down your throat—the bad-tasting liquid makes you feel ill. You send it out of your mouth, and take in large gulps of water to get free of the bad taste.

42.text: Your Kai sense gives you warning that the narrow street has no way out. If you take that way out from the square, you will certainly be kept inside. Only two other selections keep: the high gate with metal nails to your left, or the broad way straight before you.

43.text: You come to a small room set over the deep hole. Here, at least, it is dry, though the bad sewer gas goes through everything. You go in a hurry along a narrow way, which turns first to the west and then to the south, but your heart goes down as you see a wall with no way out coming out of the dark ink-black space.

44.text:
You go in a hurry through the west door and into the pleasing cold of the long room past it. A large locking bar on the inside of the door takes your eye; you lock it to delay any who would come after you.
At the end of the long room is a great hall full of instruments of war. Rows of long pointed sticks and blades are on the room walls, and a massive work table covers the floor. It is the palace room of arms. In the middle of the tools which lie about the work table, there is a large, black, skin-bound book.

45.text: You put all your Mindblast power on the guard’s hand. He gives a loud cry and his fingers open wide as his hand has all feeling and control taken from it. He is now without arms.

46.text: As your enemy comes down to the earth, the other guard makes a cut at you with his three-pointed stick. You cannot get away from the fight and must fight him till death.

47.text: You have a strong feeling that more Walasi occupy the north deep hole. You sense a resting place. It would be almost death to go that way, so you must take one of the other ways.

48.text: You put your eyes on the lock and put all your Kai power on opening it. Drops of water start to come down your face.

49.text:
The outer wall of the Great Palace is much too high to go up, and even if you had a cord long enough, your green Kai coat would be seen from miles away, placed against the white marble wall made dry by the sun.
You keep low in the dark space of a door while you put your mind to making a design. There is a constant coming and going of men on horses and messenger boys from the north door in the wall. Those who come give a paper roll to two of the guards before they enter. Slowly, a bold design starts to take form in your mind. If you could take one of the messengers before he comes to the palace door in the wall, you could put on his clothes and use his paper roll to get in.
Many of the messengers come near the Great Palace from the harbour, and though it is full of men of war, you uncover the best place to make an attack on a rider. There is a broad street where a arch of old twisted wood and metal goes over the street, and here, under the wooden arch, you lie waiting for your animal.
Your chance soon comes; a rider in black clothes comes into the street and makes his horse go fast. He will have to go under the arch. You get ready to jump.

50.text:
The smooth skin bottoms of your boots do not hold on the wet wood. You slip, and as you come down you make a cut on your head on the row of wood oars. You lose 2 ENDURANCE points.
You are taken out of the water by the Sanasim; they drag you by your coat across the sun-bleached flagstones of the harbour square and put you at Mawu’s feet. He looks at you with a cold laugh. ‘You are bold, Kai Lord. But you will have need of more than heart to keep you safe now.’

51.text:
A smooth steps-ladder goes down into the dark shaft full of bad smell. You take a deep breath of air and go down, locking the door over your head after you. When you at last come to the bottom of the shaft, your worst fears are made certain.
You have gone into the Paka-Talu, the main waste water pipe of Palakesi. You keep in mind one of the boatmen on the ship, an old man named ‘The Stink’ because he had such a bad smell, having been put in prison for one year in the Paka-Talu for a wrong he did not do. Looking along the dark holes, you wonder how he kept living for so long in this wet, dirty place.
Suddenly your thoughts are broken by the sound of breaking wood. Bits of broken wood rain down on you as the Sanasim force open the upper door. The heavy iron frame hits off your shoulder as it comes down; you keep back a cry of pain, but you lose 1 ENDURANCE point because of the wound.
This part of the Paka-Talu is a place where three water ways come together. You must quickly make a decision which way to take, for Mawu’s men are now coming down the ladder.

52.text: You turn the body over with the front of your boot and look through the loose clothing, finding 4 Gold Crowns, Keys of the Guard, a small Knife, and a long Blade.

53.text: You know the sign of the fish. It is the sign of a group of religious men named ‘The Lilima’, a quiet group who give their lives to prayer, holy journeys, and the study of the arts of making well.

54.text:
Going in a hurry down the steps and away from the Bath Hall, you go into the ‘Sati-Ta-Uta’: the Square of the Dead. Black stones cover the square, every one with a long iron needle set deep into its middle. From the Bath Hall steps, the square looks like the back of a massive iron animal with sharp points, but when you come to the base of the steps, you see that the Sati-Ta-Uta is in fact much more evil.
Put on top of every iron needle is a head of a man—all that keeps of sea-robbers, dead-makers, traitors, and thieves who have been given the punishment of death. The cruel display is a warning to others never to go against the rule of the Sakan.
As you come to the far side of the square, you brush against an iron needle. Red liquid is put on the arm of your coat, making it dark red. You put your eyes up, saying angry words at your bad chance, but you are shocked into silence by the sight before you.
Put through on the sharp iron pole is the head of the Pasakoni messenger. To every side are the heads of all the boat men. On every one of their heads is a newly burned word—TRAITOR. Fear comes up inside you; turning your face away from the eyes that do not see, you run into the full streets of the Mikalun, the place where the traders in sweet power and plants keep their houses.
At the end of a narrow, twisting street, you come to a junction. On the other side is a store with a bright red sign over the door:
Pila Ta Mason—PLANT-WOMAN

55.text:
The heat goes up steadily till you are covered in water drops. Ahead, you see a room full of warm gas that comes up from its bubbling floor. You are about to go into the room when you catch a view of the danger waiting for you; the stone walk comes to a sudden end, only a few yards into the room. Ten feet below, lying before you like the face of a huge bubbling pot, is a Ta-Soka: a soft earth fountain.
These earth fountains are common in Pasakonia. Much of the dry land empire is not solid, but though it is subject to constant earth movements, it rarely gives great destruction. The Pasakoni people give these movements the name: ‘Tasa-Topijen’, which has the sense of ‘The Fighting Gods’.
This special earth fountain has been put to practical use. It gives a constant origin of heat for the houses built over the room. The warm gas from the Ta-Soka goes up into a pair of huge, round smoke-pipes in the domed ceiling, which in turn give heat to the buildings above. Your only way out of this room is by going up one of these smoke-pipes. Though there are no ladders, the stone wall of the room gives many foot-places.

56.text:
A search of the baskets crowding the small boat uncovers a beautifully hand-made skin box. You open the brass lock and see that the box holds a Sakan—a hunting bow used by the sea fishermen of Pasakonia. You are very happy with your find but sad to see that the box holds only one Arrow.
Across the harbour square, near to Mawu’s carriage, you see a small, white-walled store where a row of green glass bottles line an open floor on the first level. You pull the bow cord to your lips and take careful aim; it is a hard shot, and you have only one chance.

57.text:
The door is not locked, and for a short time your heart goes down; if this room is the Imperial Store of Medical Plants where the Ete plant is kept, why is the door not locked and guarded? With fear you slip inside and look over the interior.
It seems to be a medical plant store. Glass instruments bubble and make gas over small blue flames, and strange liquids go back and forth through a crazy network of tubes and holes. Hundreds of plant pots line the far wall, and ten large copper pots, every one full of rainbow-coloured powder, hang suspended from the black ceiling. You start looking through the plant pots, and suddenly you see why the door was left unlocked. Coming slowly to you is the cat-like beast that guards the store. Its eyes give a bright green light as it gets ready to make an attack.

58.text: You go after a straight way of clear, rose-coloured stone, which soon comes to an end at an empty waiting room. In its north wall is set a great wooden door, covered with cut metal plates and filled with metal nails. There is a strange lock set into the middle of this door, with a circle formed by a beautiful carving of a long-tailed scorpion. A closer look at the lock shows a row of Pasakoni numbers, from 1 to 200, cut in the lock. You know the design: it is a Kolasiya combination lock.

59.text: You jump forward and hit your hand hard into the guard’s face; he makes a sound and comes down, holding a bleeding nose. His blade comes down to the earth close by your feet.

60.text:
You jump to the first man of war, making a false blow that makes him move quick to the left. You see his move before and take him in mid-step. He bends over and then comes down into the wet dirt water, holding his wound. The others wait and then step back.
Suddenly a voice comes along the deep hole. ‘Let me have him, you foolish ones!’ Mawu comes out from the dark, a small sharp stick held high in his hand. He makes a bad snake sound and sends the stick at your chest.

61.text: Suddenly, the door breaks open, and in come the Sanasim. You make a fast run for the open window but are taken from behind and pulled to the earth. Hitting out with your feet and hands you make yourself free, only to be overcome by more of the dark-skinned men of war. As they drag you out into the open space, you catch a view of the man who opened the gate; he gives a smile at you as he puts a small bag of silver into his pocket.

62.text: Feeling and experience give you warning that it would be unwise to make an attack on the guards so close to a full room of eating men; any noise of fight would straight away be heard by the men of war inside. There is now only one way for you to take—you must keep out of sight outside on the shelf going around a palace wall.

63.text: You tear long bits of cloth from your Kai coat and put them round the wound as well as you can. You manage to stop the flow, but you have lost much blood and have fear that the wound is bad with poison.

64.text: You have hard taken twelve steps along the walk when you hear a low, non-human growl. Then, the noise suddenly changes to a bad and high sound, as the huge body of a Walasi comes out from the dark. It is on you before you can take any action to get away.

65.text: The guard comes down to the earth, his neck broken by the blow from the side of your hand, but as you turn you see that the other man has got well from your hit and is moving on his hands and knees across the floor, his hand out to take back his blade.

66.text: A sour-faced guard with a whip stands at the great doors to the room for cooking food. He takes pleasure in being cruel to the slaves that go back and forth, hitting them with his whip and saying bad words to them. You make a decision that it is much too dangerous to face the guard and instead put your attention on the cooking room windows. The guard is too engrossed in hitting an unhappy slave who has dropped a basket of fruit to see you run across the gardens and jump into the dark space of a tall, arched kitchen window. Then, to your fear, you see that two guards are seated inside the cooking room, just under the window shelf on which you now stand. If they should make so much as a turn of their heads, you will be seen.

67.text:
You hear a small sound followed by a soft turning noise; the metal door slides open. As you go in a hurry through, the door closes with a small sound behind your back, as softly as it had opened.
Your inner feeling tells you that you have gone into the rooms of the higher palace, the rich private land of the Sakan. You walk on shining tiles of opal and platinum, past forms and stone pictures of clear gold. The door of solid purple stone ahead seems plain in comparison to the great beauty of this private world. Past the door lies another special and wonderfully beautiful world: the tree garden. A round arena like a great church spreads out below you, the green canopy full of the sound of bird songs. Trees of every colour, form, and size do well in the deep, dark earth of the floor. The Sakan’s tree garden has an example of every tree that grows in Malaman, and many kinds that are now no more in other places. As you walk the iron balcony which goes around the tree garden, you know the leaves of a Somelen oak. You have a sudden wave of desire for home, but it does not make you give up hope; it makes new your decision to get away from this cold-hearted, sun-bleached land.
At one of the ways out from the tree garden, you uncover a long wood stick placed against the wall. The desire to get away forces you on as you go away from the tree garden and go in a hurry through a network of rich ways and empty waiting rooms. You come to a floor space where a broad flight of steps goes down to a massive room that takes up most of the lower palace.
From the top of the steps, out of sight in the dark space of a stone pillar, you look down on a sight that makes your blood cold with fear.

68.text:
You move open the curtain of small round balls hanging in the door way and go into the cool interior. The life-less arm that hangs without power by your side has taken a blue color. Fear comes back; you must find the Ete plant to make well the disease, or you will lose the full arm and possibly your life.
A woman comes out from the dark of the store table. She has sharp green eyes and her red hair is put up, bound round with rings of Saten. ‘Welcome, North-man,’ she says, in a voice both soft and clear. ‘How may I be of use to you?’
You wait a little before answering, ‘Ete.’
She makes her eyes small and takes a look at your bad arm. ‘I cannot give you help,’ she says with grief. ‘Ete is now a very rare and high-value plant. I would have to give my store and all my things for money to get just one small bag of Ete. There is only one man in Palakesi rich enough to have this plant—the Sakan.’
Water comes out on your head as your fear grows. ‘What little Ete there is,’ she goes on, ‘is kept in the Great Palace under lock and key.’
You put the question if there is any other plant that can make well your arm. She moves her head from side to side. ‘Only Ete will make well Limb-death—and you can only find that in the strong-room of the Imperial Store of Medical Plants.’ She gets behind the store table and brings forward three glass bottles, every one holding a colored liquid. ‘They will not make you well, but they will make the pain less in the last few hours.’
